title: Digital Accessibility QA
outcome: Audit a real product against WCAG using assistive technology yourself, write findings a development team can act on, and drive the fix through an organisation.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.outcome: Know what accessibility QA is, how the standards are structured, and why an automated scan finds only a fraction of what matters.

modules.name: What Accessibility QA Actually Is
modules.objective: Describe what an accessibility reviewer produces, who consumes it, and why lived experience changes the output.
lessons: The job: finding what stops someone finishing the task
Automated scan, manual audit, user testing: three different things
Why a reviewer who uses the tech finds different bugs
Who reads an audit, and what they need from it
Doing this work at variable capacity
practice: Classify eight findings by the method that would catch them
lab: Write your own reviewer profile
A profile naming which assistive tech you use, at what level, and where you'd need a co-reviewer

modules.name: How Barriers Get Built
modules.objective: Explain why a barrier is a property of the design, not of the person meeting it.
lessons: Impairment, barrier, disability: three different words
The range of access needs one product has to serve
Situational, temporary and fluctuating access needs
Cognitive and energy-limited access, routinely forgotten
Where designers acquire the assumptions that cause barriers
practice: Reframe eight findings from deficit to barrier language
lab: Map the access needs one real product must serve
A needs map with a concrete failure example per need

modules.name: Reading WCAG Properly
modules.objective: Navigate WCAG's structure and cite the criterion that actually applies to a finding.
lessons: Principles, guidelines, criteria, techniques: what each is for
Levels A, AA, AAA and what conformance claims mean
Understanding documents and techniques: advisory, not law
Citing the right criterion instead of the nearest one
practice: Cite the governing criterion for eight findings
lab: Build your own working WCAG reference
A personal reference for the twenty criteria you'll cite most, in your own words

modules.name: The Law Behind the Standard
modules.objective: Know which legal frameworks make accessibility mandatory, and what they actually require.
lessons: Why a company is asking for this audit at all
European requirements: EN 301 549 and the Accessibility Act
US requirements: the ADA and Section 508
Accessibility statements and what makes one dishonest
Procurement: where accessibility gets decided before design
practice: Identify the governing requirement in seven scenarios
lab: Review a real accessibility statement against its product
A review naming every claim in the statement that isn't true

modules.name: What Automated Testing Can and Can't Find
modules.objective: Run automated tooling, read its output critically, and state what it left untested.
lessons: Running axe, Lighthouse and a browser inspector
The share of real barriers a scanner can detect
False positives, and the finding that isn't one
Passing the scan and failing the user
Automated checks in CI: worth having, easy to over-trust
practice: Triage eight scanner results as real, false or unknown
lab: Scan a real site, then find what the scan missed
A scan report annotated with confirmed, dismissed and additional manual findings

phases.name: Assistive Technology Fluency
phases.outcome: Operate screen readers, magnification, switch and voice control well enough to review with them rather than about them.

modules.name: Keyboard-Only Operation
modules.objective: Complete real tasks with no pointing device, and diagnose what breaks when you can't.
lessons: Tab, focus and the order nobody designed
Focus visibility, and the outline someone removed
Keyboard traps and how to recognise one fast
Skip links, landmarks and getting past the navigation
Custom controls that swallow the keyboard
practice: Complete eight tasks keyboard-only and log the breakages
lab: Keyboard-audit a full transactional flow
A flow audit with every keyboard barrier, its location and its severity

modules.name: Screen Readers: Actually Using One
modules.objective: Navigate a page with a screen reader using the commands real users navigate with.
lessons: Setting up NVDA or VoiceOver and surviving the first hour
Browse mode, focus mode, and why things stop responding
Navigating by heading, landmark, link and form field
The rotor, elements lists, and how people really move
practice: Find eight page facts using screen reader navigation only
lab: Complete a purchase flow with the screen reader alone
A transcript of what was announced at each step, with every gap marked

modules.name: Semantics, Roles and the Accessibility Tree
modules.objective: Read the accessibility tree and explain why an element is announced the way it is.
lessons: What the browser exposes, and to whom
Native elements versus div with a click handler
Name, role, value: the three things every control owes
ARIA that helps, and ARIA that overrides something correct
Inspecting the tree in browser devtools
practice: Predict the announcement for eight markup snippets
lab: Audit a component library's accessibility tree
A component-by-component report of name, role and value with the defects named

modules.name: Magnification, Zoom and Low Vision
modules.objective: Review a product the way someone using 400% zoom or a magnifier actually experiences it.
lessons: Zoom, reflow and the horizontal scrollbar that shouldn't exist
Text spacing overrides and layouts that shatter
Contrast: measuring it, and the cases the ratio misses
Using a magnifier: context loss and the off-screen change
High contrast and forced colours modes
practice: Test eight layouts at 400% and record the failures
lab: Run a full low-vision pass on a real product
A pass report covering zoom, reflow, spacing, contrast and forced colours

modules.name: Switch Access and Voice Control
modules.objective: Review for input methods that are slow, imprecise, or entirely speech-driven.
lessons: Switch scanning: every extra control costs real time
Target size, spacing and motor precision
Voice control: you can only click what has a name you can say
Timeouts that assume a fast user
Drag, hover and gestures with no alternative
practice: Find the input barrier in eight interfaces
lab: Review one interface for switch and voice operation
A review naming every unnameable control and every timing barrier

phases.name: Cognitive, Content and Energy Accessibility
phases.outcome: Find the barriers that WCAG covers thinly — cognitive load, unclear content, and interfaces that cost more energy than a person has.

modules.name: Cognitive Accessibility
modules.objective: Identify barriers created by memory demand, complexity and unpredictability.
lessons: What a form asks you to hold in your head
Consistency, predictability and the interface that moves
Instructions that arrive after the mistake
Limited attention and memory as a design constraint
practice: Find the cognitive barrier in eight flows
lab: Audit a multi-step form for cognitive load
An audit with memory demand, recovery paths and specific reductions proposed

modules.name: Content, Language and Reading
modules.objective: Judge whether the words in an interface can be understood by the people who have to use it.
lessons: Link text, button text and "click here"
Error messages that say what to do next
Reading level, jargon and the audience you actually have
Alt text: what to write when the image carries meaning
practice: Rewrite eight pieces of interface copy
lab: Rewrite the content of one complete flow
A rewritten flow with before-and-after copy and the reasoning per change

modules.name: Motion, Sound and Sensory Load
modules.objective: Find sensory barriers, including the ones that cause physical symptoms rather than inconvenience.
lessons: Animation, vestibular symptoms and reduced-motion preferences
Auto-play, carousels and things that move without asking
Flashing content and seizure risk: the actual thresholds
Audio, captions and transcripts done properly
Visual noise and interfaces that are exhausting to parse
practice: Assess eight interfaces for sensory barriers
lab: Run a sensory-load review of a media-heavy page
A review covering motion, autoplay, flash thresholds, captions and visual density

modules.name: Interaction Cost: What a Task Really Demands
modules.objective: Measure how much a task costs a user who has a limited budget of effort, and argue it as a real finding.
lessons: Counting the interactions a task actually requires
Session timeouts and the user who steps away
Work the interface makes you redo
Writing an energy-cost finding that survives "that's not WCAG"
practice: Count and reduce the interaction cost of seven tasks
lab: Produce an energy-cost audit of a core user journey
An audit with interaction counts, session risks and concrete reductions

modules.name: Trauma-Informed and Dignity-Preserving Design
modules.objective: Find design choices that are technically accessible and still humiliating or coercive.
lessons: Forms that demand more than they need
Disclosure, medical questions and who sees the answer
Dark patterns aimed at people who are tired
Language that blames the user for a system failure
Accessible and still degrading: naming it in an audit
practice: Judge eight designs for dignity as well as conformance
lab: Review a sensitive intake flow
A review naming every unnecessary disclosure and coercive pattern, with alternatives

phases.name: Running a Real Audit
phases.outcome: Scope, execute, evidence, rate and report a full audit that a development team can work from.

modules.name: Scoping an Audit
modules.objective: Define what will be tested, how, and what the audit deliberately does not cover.
lessons: Pages versus journeys: choosing the sample
Representative sampling of a large site
Choosing the test matrix: browsers, tech, platforms
Scoping to fit the hours you actually have
Writing exclusions the client agrees to in advance
practice: Scope seven audits under different constraints
lab: Write a full audit scope for a real product
A scope document with sample, matrix, method, exclusions and effort estimate

modules.name: Evidence That Holds Up
modules.objective: Capture evidence for a finding so a developer can reproduce it without you.
lessons: Reproduction steps for a screen reader finding
Recording the environment: version, platform, settings
The finding that only reproduces sometimes
Keeping evidence organised across a long audit
practice: Write reproduction steps for eight findings
lab: Evidence a full set of findings to developer standard
An evidence pack a developer could reproduce every finding from

modules.name: Severity and Prioritisation
modules.objective: Rate findings so the most harmful get fixed first, and defend the rating.
lessons: Impact, frequency, and whether there's a workaround
The blocker: nobody using this tech can finish the task
One root cause behind forty findings
Defending a rating a product owner disputes
practice: Rate and defend severity for eight findings
lab: Prioritise a hundred-finding backlog
A prioritised backlog grouped by root cause with a stated rating rationale

modules.name: Writing the Report
modules.objective: Write an audit that a developer can act on and an executive can understand.
lessons: The report structure that gets read
A finding: what, where, who it affects, what to do
Recommending a fix without designing it for them
The executive summary that doesn't lie by omission
Reports that don't shame the team who wrote the code
practice: Rewrite eight unusable findings into actionable ones
lab: Write a complete audit report
A full report: summary, method, scope, findings with evidence, severities and recommendations

modules.name: Retesting and Regression
modules.objective: Verify fixes actually fixed the barrier, and stop it coming back.
lessons: Verifying a fix rather than trusting the ticket
The fix that resolved the symptom and not the cause
Regression: barriers that return three sprints later
Reporting a retest without relitigating the audit
practice: Verify or reject eight claimed fixes
lab: Run a full retest cycle on a fixed audit
A retest report marking each finding fixed, partial or unfixed with evidence

phases.name: Advocacy and Organisational Change
phases.outcome: Turn findings into shipped fixes, and accessibility from a project into a practice.

modules.name: Why Correct Findings Don't Get Fixed
modules.objective: Diagnose the organisational reasons an accurate audit produces no change.
lessons: The audit that sat in a drive for a year
Nobody owns it: the accountability gap
Competing with the roadmap on the roadmap's terms
Compliance theatre and how to recognise it early
Finding the person who can actually decide
practice: Diagnose the blocker in seven stalled programmes
lab: Diagnose why one real audit didn't ship
A diagnosis naming the blocker and a specific intervention

modules.name: Working With Design and Engineering
modules.objective: Give feedback developers and designers can use, at the point where it's cheap to act on.
lessons: Meeting a team where their process already is
Design review before anything is built
Pairing with a developer on a fix
Component libraries: fixing once instead of forty times
Teaching without becoming the only person who knows
practice: Rewrite seven findings as design-stage feedback
lab: Run an accessibility review of a design before build
A design review with issues caught pre-build and the build cost avoided

modules.name: Making the Case Internally
modules.objective: Argue for accessibility work in the terms the person holding the budget uses.
lessons: Legal risk, market reach and cost of late fixes
Numbers you can defend, and the ones you can't
Writing for the executive who will forward it
Using your own experience without becoming the exhibit
practice: Rewrite seven weak arguments for a budget holder
lab: Write a business case for an accessibility programme
A one-page case with cost, risk, reach and a specific first ask

modules.name: From Project to Practice
modules.objective: Design the process changes that stop barriers being built in the first place.
lessons: Where accessibility fits in a delivery process
Automated checks in CI, honestly scoped
Involving disabled users, paid and properly
Maturity models and where a team actually is
practice: Place the right intervention in seven delivery processes
lab: Design an accessibility process for one real team
A process design with roles, gates, tooling and a first-90-days plan

modules.name: Capstone — A Full Audit and Its Aftermath
modules.objective: Deliver a complete audit of a real product and the plan that gets it fixed.
lessons: Choosing a product and scoping honestly
Running the audit across your own capacity
Findings, evidence and severity under real volume
Writing the report and the remediation plan
practice: Defend seven of your findings against pushback
lab: Deliver the capstone audit and remediation plan
A complete audit report, evidence pack, prioritised backlog and remediation plan

phases.name: Working in Accessibility
phases.outcome: Get and hold accessibility work — employed, contract or freelance — sustainably.

modules.name: Where the Work Is
modules.objective: Understand the shape of the accessibility job market and which route fits you.
lessons: Who hires accessibility reviewers, and why now
practice: Match seven career situations to a route
lab: Research and document your target market
A market document with ten real employers and what each screens for

modules.name: Certifications and Proof
modules.objective: Decide which credentials are worth your money and time, and what to build instead.
lessons: The certification landscape and what each signals
Cost, renewal and whether employers require it
Publishing an audit of a public site, ethically
practice: Choose a proof strategy for seven situations
lab: Publish one public work sample
A published audit or contribution, with the ethics of publishing it considered

modules.name: Getting Hired
modules.objective: Handle the practical assessment and the judgement questions in accessibility hiring.
lessons: The take-home audit task and how it's marked
Talking through an audit out loud
Interviewing while disabled, and what you owe nobody
Assessing whether they'd be a decent employer
practice: Answer seven hiring questions out loud
lab: Complete a mock take-home audit under real constraints
A completed take-home with a self-assessment against likely marking criteria

modules.name: Sustainable Practice
modules.objective: Structure the work so it doesn't cost more than it pays, physically or emotionally.
lessons: Auditing in stages that fit a real energy budget
The emotional cost of finding the same barrier repeatedly
Being the only disabled person in the room
Choosing clients who will actually fix things
practice: Redesign seven engagements for sustainability
lab: Write your own working agreement
A working agreement covering pace, scope, unpaid asks and what you decline

modules.name: Staying Current
modules.objective: Track standards, assistive tech and platform changes on a small fixed budget of time.
lessons: WCAG versions and what actually changed
Assistive tech updates that change your findings
Platform and browser changes worth watching
practice: Assess the impact of seven standard and tooling changes
lab: Run one quarterly currency review
A review naming what changed, what you retested, and which findings it revises
